Multi-line source cells are split into array elements at the source's own paragraph and line breaks; each element is verbatim. A cell that is blank in the source is recorded as null.

courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with foundational knowledge in chemistry. The course content encompasses basic concepts, including units and measurements, the atomic theory, principles of stoichiometry, properties of aqueous solutions, behaviors of gasses, thermochemistry, quantum numbers, periodic trends, chemical bonding, VSEPR theory, and the classification of organic compounds.
objectives: Establish a foundational understanding of general chemistry principles, including atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, solutions, gases, thermochemistry, etc.
Enhance problem-solving skills and critical thinking.
Foster practical skills and teamwork in the laboratory setting.
Prepare students for effective engagement in advanced courses.

clos.clo_text: Recognize the basic concepts, theoretical fundamentals, and the related experimental applications in chemistry.
Predict the solution of the problem, apply suitable strategy to reach the solution, test the correctness of the solution, and interpret the results.
Apply the principles of stoichiometry in different types of chemical reactions including reactions of aqueous solutions
Realize the main principles of thermochemistry, gases, and chemical kinetics.
Interpret periodicity concepts, distinguish the types of chemical bonding, and estimate the Lewis structure and molecular geometry of different chemical compounds.
Differentiate between the major classes of organic compounds and understand the IUPAC nomenclature of simple organic compounds.

Use different experimental techniques and work within a group in the laboratory, understand the objectives of the experiments, analyze data, and interpret results for deep understanding of the theoretical topics.

courses.description: This course introduces the principles of mechanics, energy, and heat. The course covers physics and measurement, motion in one dimension, vectors, motion in two dimensions, laws of motion, circular motion and other applications of Newton's laws, work and energy, potential energy, and conservation of energy, momentum and collisions, rotational kinematic and torque, temperature, and heat. The emphasis in this course is cultivating an understanding of natural phenomena through direct observation, reasoning, and application of this knowledge.

courses.description: This course includes several topics in electricity, magnetism, and optics. topics.topic_title:
Ch19: Electric charges, Forces and Fields.
Electric charge, Insulators and conductors, Coulombs’ Law. The electric field lines and electric fields due to symmetric charge configurations. Induction. Electric flux and Gauss’ Law.

Ch 20: Electric potential and Electric potential Energy.
Electric potential Energy and Electric potential. Energy conservation. The electric potential due to a point charge and other symmetrical charge configurations. Equipotential surfaces and the electric field. Capacitors and dielectrics. Electrical energy storage.

Ch 21: Electric Current and Direct Current Circuits.
Electric current. Resistance and Ohms’ Law. Energy and Power in Electric Circuits.
Resistors in series and in parallel. Kirchhoff’s Rules. Capacitors circuits. RC circuits.

Ch 22: Magnetism.
The magnetic fields. The Magnetic force exerted on a current carrying conductor. The magnetic force on moving charges. Electric currents, Magnetic fields, and Amperes’ Law. Current loops, Solenoid and Torrid.

Ch 23: Magnetic Flux and Faraday's Law of Induction.
Induced Electromotive force. Magnetic Flux. Faradays’ Law of Induction.

Ch 26: Geometrical Optics.
The reflection of Light. Image formation by plane mirror. Spherical mirrors. The Mirror equation and Image formation. Magnification.

courses.description: Introduction to Statistics & Probability Theory is the first course in Statistics, designed to expose the students to the use of tables and graphs as a way to summarize data and provide concise and meaningful presentations for the data. Using the computing facilities at campus, problem-solving is spreadsheet-oriented whenever possible. Excel is a spreadsheet tool for manipulating quantitative data. The extent to which the variables are related is discussed deeply through graphs and using rules. The emphasis is on analyzing, understanding, and using statistics to solve real-world problems. Coverage of the course includes descriptive statistics, probability and probability distributions, and sampling.

objectives.preamble: By the end of the semester, each student is expected to:
statements: 1. Distinguish between Population and sample; parameter and statistic, Recognize types of sampling designs and Types of variable.
2. Construct and Interpret Frequency Distribution, cumulative frequency distribution.
3. Interpret graphical summary of data sets such as box plot, histograms, stem plot, bar chart, pie charts, etc.
4. Apply concepts of descriptive statistics (Mean, Median, Mode) to solve problems.
5. Calculate Measures of location and Dispersion, and study correlation coefficient and interpret it meaning.
6. Learn basic concepts of Probability and random variables, and different rules of probability and learn how to apply them.
7. Understands the Empirical rule and Tchebysheff’s Theorem and its applications.
8. Learn how to find the Probabilities of discrete and continuous random variables using formula and statistical tables.
9. An understanding of Central Limit Theorem, and the difference between point and interval estimation
10. Understanding sampling distribution and estimating single population parameters.
